title_en: Fuzhou City People's Procuratorate v. Peng Song — intentional homicide case
ruling_gist_en: A person who, due to mental abnormality caused by drug use, commits acts harmful to society that constitute a crime shall bear criminal liability in accordance with law.
keywords_en: criminal; intentional homicide; first instance; intermediate people's court; Fujian Province; natural person; criminal law; criminal capacity after drug use; constitution of intentional homicide; support for plaintiff; drug use; stabbing with knife; causing death; voluntary surrender
full_text_en:
Fuzhou Municipal People's Procuratorate v. Peng Song — intentional homicide

Ruling Summary

Where a person, due to abnormal mental state caused by drug use, commits an act harmful to society that constitutes a crime, he shall bear criminal liability according to law.

Prosecutorial Authority: Fujian Province Fuzhou Municipal People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Peng Song, male, 23 years old, unemployed, residing at Shanyang Village, Shanyang Town, Gutian County, Fujian Province. He was detained on suspicion of intentional homicide on May 6, 2005, and arrested on June 10 of the same year.

Civil Plaintiff (Collateral to Criminal Proceedings): Ruan Xiangjin, male, 54 years old, farmer, residing at Zouyang Village, Dajia Township, Datian County, Fujian Province, father of the victim Ruan Zhaosen.

Civil Plaintiff (Collateral to Criminal Proceedings): Li Fengyu, female, 50 years old, farmer, residing at the same address as Ruan Xiangjin, mother of the victim Ruan Zhaosen.

The Fujian Province Fuzhou Municipal People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against the defendant Peng Song for intentional homicide before the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province. The victim Ruan Zhaosen's father, Ruan Xiangjin, and mother, Li Fengyu, as civil plaintiffs in the collateral civil action, initiated a civil action collateral to the criminal proceedings before the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province.

The indictment alleged: On the early morning of May 5, 2005, after the effects of the ecstasy pill he had taken took hold, the defendant Peng Song, in Room 204, Building 6, Beijiangli New Village, Gulou District, Fuzhou, where he was temporarily staying, stabbed the victim Ruan Zhaosen, who shared the room, in the chest with a knife. Ruan Zhaosen died despite rescue efforts. Forensic medical examination determined that Ruan Zhaosen died from massive hemorrhage due to liver laceration caused by a single-edged sharp instrument piercing his left chest. At approximately 21:00 on the same day, Peng Song voluntarily surrendered to the Major Case Unit of the Criminal Investigation Detachment of the Ningde Municipal Public Security Bureau, Fujian Province. Peng Song's conduct constituted the crime of intentional homicide, and the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court was requested to punish him according to law.

The prosecutorial authority, the Fuzhou Municipal People's Procuratorate, submitted the following evidence:

1. Testimony of witness Li Qingling (girlfriend of victim Ruan Zhaosen), stating that on the day of the incident, she, Ruan Zhaosen, and the defendant Peng Song returned to their temporary residence together. Ruan Zhaosen said to Peng Song's girlfriend, Yu Qiaomei: "Peng Song took ecstasy and is very disoriented." After Peng Song returned to the room, he slapped Yu Qiaomei twice for no reason, and Yu Qiaomei left. She saw Peng Song lying on the bed, staring at the ceiling with a vacant expression. Ruan Zhaosen gave him water to drink, but he did not drink. Later, Peng Song went to the kitchen, took a fruit knife, and brandished it at Ruan Zhaosen. Ruan Zhaosen tried to dissuade him, but Peng Song just smiled, turned, and walked toward the living room. When Ruan Zhaosen and she were about to leave, Peng Song, holding the knife with both hands, stabbed Ruan Zhaosen directly in the heart area. When he pulled the knife out, there was blood on it. After being injured, Ruan Zhaosen ran downstairs. She, out of fear, hid in the kitchen. Peng Song followed her in. She begged Peng Song not to kill her; Peng Song stopped, smiled at her, turned around, and went out to chase Ruan Zhaosen. Ruan Zhaosen and Peng Song were good friends, which was why Ruan Zhaosen had allowed Peng Song and his girlfriend to move in and stay with them. They had been living together for over ten days by the time of the incident. Ruan Zhaosen had never taken ecstasy; she had heard from Yu Qiaomei that Peng Song frequently took ecstasy.

2. Testimony of witness Yu Qiaomei, stating that at around 3:00 a.m. on May 5, 2005, the defendant Peng Song was supported back by the victim Ruan Zhaosen. His face was dark, looking somewhat terrifying. Later, Peng Song slapped her for no reason, so she left. Later, Ruan Zhaosen's girlfriend, Li Qingling, called and told her that Peng Song had stabbed Ruan Zhaosen with a knife. She rushed back to their temporary residence in Beijiangli New Village and saw Peng Song being held down by several of his friends. At that time, Li Qingling came downstairs, and together they went to look for Ruan Zhaosen. When they reached the entrance of Beijiangli New Village, a taxi driver told them he had taken Ruan Zhaosen to the Provincial Hospital. The two then took a taxi to the Provincial Hospital. She and Peng Song had been in a romantic relationship since 2000. Peng Song had told her about his ecstasy use, and she had advised him to stop. When they were together, she never saw Peng Song take ecstasy. After the incident, while she and Li Qingling were on their way to the Provincial Hospital by taxi, she heard Li Qingling say that Peng Song had taken ecstasy before the incident.

3. Testimony of witness Yu Zhiyuan, stating that at around 3:00 a.m. on the day of the incident, he heard the victim Ruan Zhaosen and the defendant Peng Song, who lived next door, return. Soon after, he heard Ruan Zhaosen saying in the living room, "We're all brothers, don't do this," followed by the sound of the iron door opening. He got up and saw that Ruan Zhaosen had already reached the doorway and was running downstairs. Peng Song, holding a fruit knife in his left hand with blood on the blade, followed him downstairs. He heard Li Qingling, Ruan Zhaosen's girlfriend, say to Ruan Zhaosen's friend "Feng Di": "Peng Song has gone crazy and stabbed Ruan Zhaosen with a knife. Now both of them have run downstairs. I'm afraid Peng Song is still at the door, so I dare not go out now. Come and see if Peng Song is still downstairs." Later, he heard Li Qingling say that Peng Song had gone stupid from drugs and gone crazy. The drug Li Qingling referred to was ecstasy.

4. Testimony of witness Ruan Xiangjin, stating that his son, the victim Ruan Zhaosen's girlfriend, came to his residence and told him that Ruan Zhaosen had been stabbed by the defendant Peng Song with a knife and taken to the hospital for rescue.

5. Confession of the defendant Peng Song, stating that at around 1:00 a.m. on May 5, 2005, he drank two bottles of beer while having a midnight snack with friends. At around 2:00 a.m., while playing at the Fuzhou Union Nightclub, he took an ecstasy pill. Afterwards, his vision blurred, and he saw many colorful wavy stripes. He felt that everyone was speaking ill of him and looking at him with contempt. He wanted to vent, and he pushed his friend "Feng Di" to the ground. After the victim Ruan Zhaosen brought him back to Room 204, No. 6, Beijiangli New Village, his temporary residence, he felt that his girlfriend Yu Qiaomei was also speaking ill of him, so he slapped her twice, and Yu Qiaomei left. At that time, he felt that his friends were conspiring against him, and he thought, "Since you're all ganging up on me, I'm not afraid. At worst, I'll lose my life. If you want to hit me, I need to find a knife to defend myself." So he went to the kitchen and found a 20-centimeter-long single-edged fruit knife. When Ruan Zhaosen told him to drink water, he raised the knife and gestured at Ruan Zhaosen, but then felt there was no need to stab Ruan Zhaosen, so he put the knife down. Ruan Zhaosen immediately ran to the door, and Ruan Zhaosen's girlfriend also ran to the kitchen. He thought that the door in the room was very close to the kitchen, and if Ruan Zhaosen took a knife from the kitchen, it would be very dangerous for him, and he would be killed by Ruan Zhaosen. So he decided to strike first. He held the knife in his right hand and stabbed Ruan Zhaosen in the chest and abdomen. Ruan Zhaosen cried out "Ouch," turned around, and ran out. He followed and ran downstairs. After the incident, he surrendered himself to the Ningde Municipal Public Security Bureau. He also confessed that he had taken ecstasy seven or eight times before and had experienced similar hallucinations after taking it.

6. Scene inspection record and scene photographs, confirming that the crime scene was located at Room 204, Building 6, Beijiangli New Village, Gulou District, Fuzhou, and that the defendant Peng Song identified the crime scene.

7. Forensic medical examination report from the Fuzhou Municipal Public Security Bureau, confirming that the victim Ruan Zhaosen died from massive hemorrhage due to liver laceration caused by a single-edged sharp instrument piercing his left chest.

8. Certificate from the Ningde Municipal Public Security Bureau, Fujian Province, confirming the process by which the defendant Peng Song voluntarily surrendered.

The defendant Peng Song and his defense counsel argued that Peng Song's conduct did not constitute the crime of intentional homicide, with the main reasons being: 1. Peng Song committed the act under a pathological motive induced by taking ecstasy. At the time of the act, his ability to recognize and control his own conduct was lost, making him a person without criminal responsibility; therefore, he should not bear criminal liability. 2. Even if Peng Song's conduct constituted a crime, it should be convicted and punished as the crime of negligent homicide. 3. Peng Song voluntarily surrendered, which could be considered for a lighter or mitigated punishment.

The civil plaintiffs (collateral to criminal proceedings) Ruan Xiangjin and Li Fengyu requested that the defendant and civil defendant (collateral to criminal proceedings) Peng Song compensate them for the victim Ruan Zhaosen's rescue costs of RMB 5,000, death compensation of RMB 81,787.6, funeral expenses of RMB 7,801.5, dependent living expenses of RMB 120,608.8, as well as lost work expenses of RMB 1,282.2, transportation expenses of RMB 1,000, and moral damages of RMB 80,000, totaling RMB 297,480.1. They also submitted relevant evidence such as household registration certificates, medical expense invoices, and transportation tickets.

The Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

On the early morning of May 5, 2005, after the effects of the ecstasy pill he had taken took hold, the defendant Peng Song, in Room 204, Building 6, Beijiangli New Village, Gulou District, Fuzhou, where he was temporarily staying, stabbed the victim Ruan Zhaosen, who shared the room, in the chest with a knife, resulting in Ruan Zhaosen's death despite rescue efforts. Forensic medical examination determined that Ruan Zhaosen died from massive hemorrhage due to liver laceration caused by a single-edged sharp instrument piercing his left chest. At approximately 9:00 p.m. on the same day, Peng Song surrendered himself to the Ningde Municipal Public Security Bureau, Fujian Province.

It was also found that the defendant Peng Song's conduct caused certain economic losses to the civil plaintiffs (collateral to criminal proceedings) Ruan Xiangjin and Li Fengyu. The claims of Ruan Xiangjin and Li Fengyu for compensation from Peng Song for death compensation of RMB 81,787.6, funeral expenses of RMB 7,801.5, and transportation expenses of RMB 1,000 were supported by factual evidence and were in accordance with relevant legal provisions. Ruan Xiangjin and Li Fengyu requested that Peng Song compensate for the victim Ruan Zhaosen's dependent living expenses, but failed to provide evidence that the dependents had lost the ability to work and had no other sources of livelihood. Their claim for compensation for Ruan Zhaosen's rescue costs was RMB 5,000, but the hospital's fee invoice indicated the rescue cost was RMB 1,392. Before the first instance trial, Peng Song's family had already paid RMB 11,000 to Ruan Zhaosen's family, and after the trial began, an additional RMB 5,000 was paid to the court.

The disputed issue to be resolved in this case was: whether the defendant Peng Song, having taken ecstasy and committed homicide under its influence, should bear criminal liability.

The Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court held in its first instance judgment:

The defendant Peng Song intentionally and unlawfully deprived another person of life, causing death. Although the homicide was committed after the effects of taking ecstasy took hold, he should bear criminal liability according to law. Therefore, the charge brought by the prosecutorial authority was established, and Peng Song's conduct constituted the crime of intentional homicide. The defenses of Peng Song and his defense counsel that Peng Song's conduct did not constitute the crime of intentional homicide were untenable. Peng Song voluntarily surrendered after the crime, and a lighter punishment could be imposed.

The death of the victim Ruan Zhaosen caused certain economic losses to the civil plaintiffs (collateral to criminal proceedings) Ruan Xiangjin and Li Fengyu. The claims of Ruan Xiangjin and Li Fengyu for compensation from the defendant Peng Song for death compensation of RMB 81,787.6, funeral expenses of RMB 7,801.5, and transportation expenses of RMB 1,000 were supported by factual evidence and were in accordance with relevant legal provisions, and should be upheld. The claims of Ruan Xiangjin and Li Fengyu for Peng Song to compensate for the victim Ruan Zhaosen's dependent living expenses, failing to provide evidence that the dependents had lost the ability to work and had no other sources of livelihood, and their claims for lost work expenses and moral damages, lacked legal basis, and were not upheld. Their claim for compensation for the victim Ruan Zhaosen's rescue costs was RMB 5,000, but the hospital's fee invoice indicated the rescue cost was RMB 1,392; therefore, the rescue cost was determined to be RMB 1,392. The total amount above was RMB 91,981.1. Before the first instance trial, Peng Song's family had already paid RMB 11,000 to Ruan Zhaosen's family, and after the trial began, an additional RMB 5,000 was paid to the court. This RMB 16,000 should be deducted from the total compensation amount. Therefore, Peng Song should still pay RMB 75,981.1 to Ruan Xiangjin and Li Fengyu.

Accordingly, the Fuzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment on May 10, 2006 as follows:

1. The defendant Peng Song is convicted of intentional homicide and sentenced to life imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for life;

2. The defendant Peng Song shall pay the civil plaintiffs (collateral to criminal proceedings) Ruan Xiangjin and Li Fengyu economic losses of RMB 91,981.1. After deducting the RMB 16,000 already paid, the defendant Peng Song shall still pay RMB 75,981.1, and shall pay this amount within three months from the effective date of this judgment.

Peng Song appealed against the first instance judgment to the Fujian High People's Court, with the main grounds being: 1. The appellant Peng Song's ability to recognize and control his conduct at the time of the crime was lost, making him a person without criminal responsibility, and he should not bear criminal liability. 2. Even if Peng Song's conduct was found to constitute a crime, it did not constitute intentional homicide, but could only be found to constitute negligent homicide. Furthermore, the appellant voluntarily surrendered, which should result in a lighter or mitigated punishment.

After the second instance trial, the Fujian High People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The Fujian High People's Court held in its second instance judgment:

The appellant Peng Song should bear criminal liability for his homicide.

First, according to the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law), a person who commits an act causing certain harmful consequences shall not bear criminal liability in the following circumstances: (1) The person who commits a criminal act prescribed by the Criminal Law has not reached the age of criminal responsibility, i.e., is under 14 years of age when committing crimes such as intentional homicide, intentional injury causing serious injury or death, rape, robbery, drug trafficking, arson, explosion, or poisoning, or is under 16 years of age when committing other crimes prescribed by the Criminal Law; (2) A mental patient causes harmful consequences when he is unable to recognize or control his own conduct, as confirmed by statutory procedures; (3) Acts of justifiable defense taken to stop an unlawful infringement that is ongoing against the State, public interest, or the person, property, or other rights of oneself or others, causing harm to the infringer but not exceeding the necessary limits; (4) Acts of necessity taken to avert an imminent danger to the State, public interest, or the person, property, or other rights of oneself or others, causing harm but not exceeding the necessary limits. The appellant Peng Song, after the effects of taking ecstasy took hold, committed homicide, causing the death of the victim Ruan Zhaosen. His conduct was seriously harmful to society and clearly did not fall within the above circumstances prescribed by the Criminal Law for exemption from criminal liability.

Second, the appellant Peng Song did not suffer from any mental illness. The temporary abnormal mental state after taking ecstasy is essentially the same as the temporary abnormal mental state after intoxication. Article 18 of the Criminal Law provides: "A person who commits a crime while intoxicated shall bear criminal liability." According to this provision, a person who commits a crime due to a temporary abnormal mental state after intoxication shall bear criminal liability. Therefore, a person who commits a crime due to a temporary abnormal mental state after drug use shall also bear criminal liability.

Third, drug use, including the use of ecstasy, is an illegal act. The appellant Peng Song had taken ecstasy many times before and had experienced hallucinations after taking it. Peng Song was fully aware of this. On the night of the incident, as a person with normal capacity for conduct, knowing that taking drugs would cause a temporary abnormal mental state, Peng Song nevertheless voluntarily took ecstasy, ultimately leading to an abnormal mental state and the commission of homicide. It was precisely Peng Song's voluntary drug use that caused him to fall into an abnormal mental state, under which he committed the criminal act, causing serious harmful consequences. Therefore, Peng Song should bear criminal liability for his conduct.

In summary, the Fujian High People's Court, pursuant to Articles 232, 67(1), and 57(1) of the Criminal Law, and Article 189(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, ordered on February 28, 2007:

Appeal dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This order is final.
